head: 462906fc
gate: HTTP/3 response stream set caches the monotonic QPACK-unblocked answer so a 32-stream batch no longer re-parses every complete message on each ready scan

commands.h3_concurrent: zig build test-lib -Dtest-filter="HTTP/3 continuous concurrent" --summary all

benchmark.workload: weft synthetic-handshake HTTP/3 server, one loopback connection, GET / -> 200 "ok", 10k sequential plus 1k x 32-stream batches

notes: ResponseStreamSet.firstReadyStream, readyEntry and blockedReadyStreamCount each re-parsed every complete buffered message with common.messageBlockedByQpack on every ready scan. With 32 outstanding streams that is O(n^2) frame parsing and QPACK prefix decoding per batch. Entry now records qpack_unblocked once a complete message is proven independent of an outstanding insert; the field section is immutable after FIN and the encoder insert count only grows, so the answer is monotonic. Measured 32-stream GET improved 152.4 -> 139.9 us/request (6.6k -> 7.2k req/s) and upload 188.1 -> 173.2 us/request. A netz-only harness (zio event loop, HandshakeServer + serveConcurrentStreams + client batch API) reproduces the same shape as weft: batch=8 49-53 us/request versus batch=32 146-153 us/request before this change. Ruled out as the 32-stream cause: worker-pool size (caps of 8 and 16 changed nothing), server pacing (raising the max pacing rate to 1 GB/s changed 146-153 to 137-143 us/request), and per-command wake latency (0.4-12 us after the wake race). Owner-loop counters show two events per request at both widths, so the remaining gap is in the client/server lockstep rather than in command dispatch.
